sources.citation: Wycliffe Bible Translators. 2017 [electronic ed. 2023]. Itlajtol Totajtzin Dios. El Nuevo Testamento en el náhuatl de la Sierra Negra de Puebla (nsu 16-042). 593 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Primary text only; front matter (pp. i-vi, prologue) and back matter (pp. 580-593) checked: no alphabet or pronunciation note. Orthography writes an acute accent on non-penultimate stressed syllables (oyá 'was', ijkí 'thus', ijkó, íkka, neká), implying default penultimate stress, but no statement.

sources.citation: Hasler, Juan A. 2011. Estudios nahuas. Xalapa: Universidad Veracruzana (Biblioteca). 256 pp. Open access, DOI 10.25009/uv.1950.73. Ch. IV 'Las palabras acentuadas en nahua' (1952-53; Archivos nahuas I.1, 1955), pp. 29-32
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: General-Nahuatl note: 'en náhuatl todas las palabras se acentúan en la penúltima sílaba' with oxytone exceptions explained as compounds/enclitics (oksé, amotlén, -tsín, -é); p. 32 explicitly EXCLUDES 'el acento esdrújulo de la región de Zongolican' (the Tehuacán-Zongolica dialect area to which nsu belongs) and never returned to it. Ch. VIII p. 64 gives a penultimate rule for Pipil of Los Tuxtlas, a different language. No Sierra Negra locality data.
